subject: Physics
topic: Newton's Laws of Motion & Momentum Systems
title: Core 1B Phenomenological Reconstruction Cycles, Cognitive Dissonance Dialog & First-Move Priming

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Coupled Multi-Body Acceleration in Atwood Machine
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Separate FBDs: m1*g - T = m1*a and T - m2*g = m2*a. Adding equations eliminates tension T: (m1 - m2)*g = (m1 + m2)*a => a = (m1 - m2)*g / (m1 + m2).

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Treat the two masses and the string as an unrolled 1D continuous chain along the string coordinate.
phenomenological_reconstruction.inertial_resistance: Total system inertia to be accelerated = (m1 + m2)
phenomenological_reconstruction.reconstructed_formula: a = \frac{\text{Net Driving Force}}{\text{Total Inertia}} = \frac{(m_1 - m_2)g}{m_1 + m_2}
phenomenological_reconstruction.tension_reconstruction: T = \frac{2 m_1 m_2}{m_1 + m_2} g \quad \text{(Harmonic mean of gravitational weights)}

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: a = 0, T = m1*g (System in neutral static equilibrium)
a -> g, T -> 2*m2*g (m1 in free fall, pulling negligible m2 upward)
a = g, T = 0 (Free fall of m1 with disconnected string)

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Inclined Plane Slip Threshold & Angle of Repose
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Project gravity: along plane F_parallel = mg*sin(theta), normal F_perp = mg*cos(theta). Normal force N = mg*cos(theta). Slip condition f_s <= mu_s * N => mg*sin(theta) <= mu_s * mg*cos(theta) => tan(theta) <= mu_s.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Combine normal reaction N and friction force f into a single total contact force vector R = N + f. For static equilibrium, R must be strictly vertical and collinear with gravity mg.
phenomenological_reconstruction.cone_angle: Maximum angle between R and surface normal is the angle of friction lambda, where tan(lambda) = f_max / N = mu_s.
phenomenological_reconstruction.equilibrium_condition: Since R is vertical, the angle of the incline theta equals the angle between R and the normal. Hence equilibrium is maintained if and only if theta <= lambda, yielding tan(theta) <= mu_s.
phenomenological_reconstruction.mass_independence: Notice mass m cancels completely: repose angle depends purely on the interface roughness, not the weight of the block.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: theta_repose = 0 deg; block slides on any non-zero incline
theta_repose = 90 deg; block never slides along surface
Driving force = 0, normal N = mg, friction f_s = 0

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Stacked Two-Block Slip Threshold on Frictionless Table
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: Block A (mass m1) rests on Block B (mass m2). Horizontal force F pulls B. Max friction on A is f_max = mu*m1*g, giving A max acceleration a_max = f_max / m1 = mu*g. For no relative slip, whole system must accelerate at <= mu*g, so F_max = (m1 + m2)*a_max = mu*(m1 + m2)*g.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: Ride in the accelerating frame of bottom block B with acceleration a. A fictitious pseudo force F_pseudo = m1*a pulls block A backward.
phenomenological_reconstruction.force_balance_on_A: Static friction f_s pushes block A forward to counter the backward pseudo force: f_s = m1*a.
phenomenological_reconstruction.slip_criterion: Block A slips when the pseudo force exceeds the maximum available friction: m1*a > mu*m1*g => a > mu*g.
phenomenological_reconstruction.whole_system_limit: Since the external force F accelerates both blocks, F = (m1 + m2)*a <= (m1 + m2)*mu*g.

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: F_max = 0; any non-zero pull causes B to slide out instantly
F_max -> mu*m1*g; inertia dominated entirely by top block

reconstruction_cycles.phenomenon: Movable Pulley Kinematic Invariant & Mechanical Advantage
reconstruction_cycles.standard_derivation: String length L = 2*y_pulley + y_load. Differentiating twice: 2*a_pulley + a_load = 0 => a_load = -2*a_pulley. Balance of forces on massless pulley: 2*T - F = 0 => T = F/2.

phenomenological_reconstruction.conceptual_pivot: An ideal machine cannot create energy: Input Work = Output Work. F * Delta x_input = W_load * Delta y_load.
phenomenological_reconstruction.kinematic_tradeoff: To lift the load by Delta y, both supporting string segments must shorten by Delta y, requiring 2*Delta y of string to be pulled at the effort end: Delta x_input = 2 * Delta y_load.
phenomenological_reconstruction.force_ratio: Hence Effort F = W_load / 2. Acceleration is halved, but lifting force is doubled (Mechanical Advantage = 2).
phenomenological_reconstruction.reconstructed_formula: W_{\text{in}} = W_{\text{out}} \implies F \cdot (2\Delta y) = W_{\text{load}} \cdot \Delta y \implies F = \frac{W_{\text{load}}}{2}

limiting_boundary_checks.physical_consequence: Mechanical advantage unchanged, but stored elastic energy reduces instantaneous work output

cognitive_dissonance_probes.scenario: A 100 kg person stands on a spring bathroom scale in a freely falling elevator (cable snapped, air resistance negligible).
cognitive_dissonance_probes.dissonance_question: What does the scale read? 100 kg, 980 N, or 0 N?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: 0 N (Apparent weightlessness). Both person and scale accelerate downward at g. No normal contact force is required to prevent relative penetration.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.scenario: A horse pulls a wagon with force F_hw = 500 N. By Newton's 3rd Law, the wagon pulls back on the horse with F_wh = 500 N. How can the wagon possibly accelerate forward if the backward pull equals the forward pull?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.dissonance_question: Why do these equal and opposite forces not produce static equilibrium?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: The forces act on DIFFERENT bodies. To determine wagon acceleration, inspect forces acting ON THE WAGON (forward pull from horse minus wheel friction). The backward pull acts ON THE HORSE, which the horse overcomes by pushing backward against the ground with its hooves.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.scenario: You apply a horizontal force of 20 N to a heavy 50 kg crate on a rough floor with static friction coefficient mu_s = 0.5. The crate remains at rest.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.dissonance_question: Is the static friction force acting on the crate 245 N (mu_s * m * g) or 20 N?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Exactly 20 N. mu_s * N = 245 N is the MAXIMUM POSSIBLE static friction threshold. Static friction matches the applied driving force exactly up to that threshold to maintain Sigma F = 0.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.scenario: A block sits at rest on the bed of an accelerating truck. As the truck speeds up forward, the block also speeds up forward without slipping relative to the truck.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.dissonance_question: Which direction does friction on the block act? Forward or backward?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: FORWARD. The only horizontal force acting on the block is static friction from the truck bed. By Newton's 2nd Law, Sigma F = m*a_forward, so friction must point in the direction of acceleration (forward).

cognitive_dissonance_probes.scenario: A 0.20 kg ball strikes a wall at 8 m/s and rebounds at 6 m/s. A student computes Delta p = 0.20*(8 - 6) = 0.40 kg m/s.
cognitive_dissonance_probes.dissonance_question: What fatal error was committed, and what is the true momentum change?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Momentum is a signed directional vector. With initial direction positive, p_i = +1.6 kg m/s and p_f = -1.2 kg m/s. Delta p = p_f - p_i = -1.2 - (+1.6) = -2.8 kg m/s. Rebound produces roughly double the momentum change.

cognitive_dissonance_probes.scenario: A 0.020 kg bullet is fired from a 2.0 kg rifle. Both acquire equal momentum magnitudes |p|. Does the shooter receive as much kinetic energy as the target?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.dissonance_question: Why is the bullet deadly while the rifle recoil is merely uncomfortable?
cognitive_dissonance_probes.resolution: Kinetic energy K = p^2 / (2m). Because momentum magnitude |p| is identical, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass. The bullet (100 times lighter) absorbs 100 times more kinetic energy than the rifle.
